answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents emit a continuous pulse of zero-knowledge proofs of ongoing computation, each chained into an immutable thread of state updates that must be attested by a grove of established high-stake validators. An attacker creating many fake agents would incur rising costs because every pulse demands fresh, non-shareable computational work and stake that cannot be reused across identities, quickly exhausting resources as the number of Sybils grows.
